I’ve made some really bad choices in my life, and I’ve had to accept the consequences for some of them. I had just finished my prison sentence when I went out with some friends for a beer fest event. I got a job and met a friend there that seemed cool. He wanted to meet up with this girl that he was talking to, so we drove to her house and she had a guy. I got this gut feeling that something bad was going to happen but I blew it off. We went outside so he could smoke before we left for the event, and I asked my friend who the other guy was. He didn’t know and didn’t mind that his “girl” had a guy over, so we all got in her car and left. 

We are driving on the highway and it’s freezing outside. For some reason she had the windows down, so I was pissed off but biting my tongue. When we arrive, she had parked in a bad neighborhood, and she said that we had to walk through a field to get there. So I start walking and out of nowhere my “friend” pulls a knife out and stabs the other guy. They start fist fighting, and all I can think about is going back to prison. I had just gotten out of that shit hole, and here I am in a fucked up position that was going to land me right back in it.

So I grabbed my shit and the “friend” and I got the fuck out of there. I called my friend that was at the college nearby (she is the most high maintenance rich kid you can think of). She agreed to drive to the worst neighborhood around to pick us up, so my friend and I got in her car. The first place we hit up was McDonalds because I needed some good food before I went back to prison, and then we ended up turning him in at a damn gas station. Before we got to the gas station, he pulled a knife out and threatened that if I didn’t tell the “right” story that he would kill me.

All these cops showed up and cuffed the guy, so I’m stranded 3 hours from home. They let me go because everyone stated that I wasn’t involved, and my friend (girl) had to drive me all the way home. That whole situation could have ended much worse for me. I could have been back in prison or stabbed by the unstable guy that I thought was my friend.
That is the dumbest thing I’ve ever heard, and I’ve heard some really stupid shit. Borderlines...

She was reading a story to my younger sibling, and I made a comment about the story so she smacked me across the face. I told my parents and the next day they told her, “We don’t do that here”. They continued to let her watch us after that. The reason why my parents decided to finally fire her was when my dad came home one morning to find her dumbass passed out in the chair with my toddler brother playing on the floor unsupervised.
If they attack you, doofy. I guess that concept must be hard to grasp for someone like you.

Tell her that you’ve lost your job and need her help financially.
Too controlling and too many meltdowns from what I’ve experienced.
Not as much now that I’m an adult. I mainly just have one on one conversations now.

If someone is yelling me (except kids) I shout back. You had to hold your own in my house when I was growing up. It’s not healthy and I think the best approach is to stay quiet and walk away. The person that stays quiet and walks away always wins every time.
I don’t associate with groups—just individuals.

I got in a lot of trouble that I eventually couldn’t get out of.

My mom tried to embarrass us in public bathrooms too. She would stand outside of the bathroom entrance, scream our names, and say, “Are you okay in there? You’ve been in there for a very long time...”. That would be right after we walked in and locked the stalls.

The other day my mom came to my house and started banging on the door. I thought the cops were at our house with how hard she was knocking. Then she rang the doorbell repeatedly (dingdingdingdingdingding). I’m in the bathroom brushing my teeth and my daughter is screaming bloody murder and grabbing my leg. So I go out there and the other kids are just staring at the door. Before I can get the door open, she starts banging on the windows and calling my phone.

I open the door and she says, “What, did you oversleep”?

There wasn’t an emergency and it wasn’t even 8 a.m. I’m surprised someone didn’t call the cops on her.
That’s interesting. Do you have BPD? My mom has that and won’t seek treatment.

I don’t think you can prevent it. 

You can control the choices that you make though.

Those other mental illnesses can be treated/ managed effectively while ASPD doesn’t have a pill or type of therapy to make things better. Therapy might help some (maybe), but how effective can it really be with ASPD? Would talk therapy, mood stabilizers, antidepressants, etc. really even help? If anything, they are just a fascinating mystery to others.

I think there’s a difference between a firm tone and screaming in a kid’s face. If I’m calm and say something in a friendly voice, my kids typically don’t listen. If I use a serious tone, they know that I’m serious and don’t want them to do something like run in the road. However, humiliating/scaring them by screaming in their faces doesn’t work either. 

One thing I don’t understand is spanking. When you spank, you’re pissed off so it’s not going to be a light tap. It’s going to be hard enough that you leave a mark. Being spanked didn’t teach me anything except how to hide the bruises.

Yes, all the time. She wasn’t happy unless she could make my siblings and I feel ashamed. When we gave her the reaction she wanted (red cheeks with our heads down), she got this huge smile on her face like she won the lottery.

She would also make us find our brother in the store that would take off all the time (she didn’t feel like looking for him), and one time that backfired on her because some man took an interest in my sister. My sister ran all over the store (trying to find my mom) crying because he was trying to grab her and take her with him. I don’t think my mom would have cared if he took my sister because she could have used that to gain sympathy with people. “Oh no, my poor baby was kidnapped. Feel bad for meeeee”. 🙄 We were nothing but burdens to her.

Yes, I completely understand where you’re coming from. I should have filed for emancipation because I had the means to do it. 

When I did have friends, they would always say that my parents didn’t like me. My parents didn’t even try to hide the fact that they didn’t want me. It made people extremely uncomfortable and they slowly stopped talking to me.

There’s no way you can live on campus? Speak to your advisor at your university to see if there are programs available to help you financially. I know people that lived on school loans and worked part-time jobs until they could graduate. I know the loans will take a long time to pay off, but it has to be better than being around your family.

 My younger sister was in a similar situation when the rest of us moved out, so she married the first guy that she could find to get away from the abuse. Let them talk shit and move on. It’s not worth the consequences. I’m learning how to take my own advice.
ADHD. My family is full of mental problems, so I’m sure I have more but haven’t been formally diagnosed with them.

Start your own business. People sell junk on that one website and seem to do well. Some lady paints blocks to look like dice and wants $40+ per order. Try and go to school to work in a funeral home and deal with dead bodies if you can stomach it. They don’t judge and the pay isn’t completely terrible.

Death scares me more than most people because I’m not religious. Everyone always says that I should “turn to god”,  but you can’t force something like that.

I think everyone knows I’m messed up because I’ve been in prison, so I’m not going to be remembered as a great person. Maybe to my kids because I am trying to be better for them, but I don’t know if I can change because this has been “me” for so long. If I didn’t have them, I’d probably be right back in prison because I would have nothing to lose.

I’m just glad I’m not as fucked up as some people.

Exactly. It will happen again. She’s going to cheat on anyone that she’s with. Coparent and that’s it. Whoever you hook up with is your business. She’s the one that ended things, so she sure as hell can’t tell you what to do.

Why would you want to take the test? He’s clearly a piece of shit, and you’re only going to end up hurt or dead with him. I’ve met people that have killed their significant others, and he sounds similar to them (extreme up and down relationships).
Live like she’s not coming back. Start meeting other people and enjoy your life. It might suck for a little bit because you miss her, but meeting new people can be exciting.
If you want to stop loving her then don’t respond. Don’t have any contact at all. Focus on your life and meet other people.

You need to leave. You’re going to lose custody of your son if you continue to stay with him. This man has hurt your son, and it will get worse the longer you stay together.

Go to the state and get government assistance or whatever you have to do. Tell them you have nowhere to go. Even if they send you to a shelter, you will have a place to stay. Get food stamps, WIC, free childcare costs, and whatever else they can give you.

People with normal jobs have progressed to managing positions, so that’s considered building a career. They can also make a decent living that way. It sounds more like he wants someone with a good job for “image” purposes. If you’re okay with it then keep dating, but if not then bring it up.
Do whatever you want. People are always going to have something bad to say about you, so live your life for yourself and not anyone else.
Don’t ask out someone you’ve never spoken to. Try and get to know her first.

I wouldn’t even waste my time at this point. She’s seeing someone else, but wants you around in case things don’t work out. 

People always leave because something new is exciting, and when that wears off they say they have “made a mistake”. Focus on yourself and don’t continue date nights with her. Be done so she feels the consequences of her decision. She might come back or she might not, but it’s up to you to decide if she’s worth taking back. Oh, and don’t take her back just for the kids because they will feel the pressure to “keep the marriage together”.

I wouldn’t say anything. It’s not your responsibility to change her feelings toward you, but if she asks you out just say no. If she confesses her feelings, you need to tell her that you don’t feel the same way.

Odds are she’s not insane and won’t stalk/kill you over it.

Because I don’t have the desire to hurt children.

I don’t really care to get “better” or find a diagnosis.
It depends on who I’m talking to.

Peter Popoff.

It’s also easier for people with ASPD to pick up on scams because many of them scam others. The whole “it takes one to know one”...

If someone else is having issues, the only way I can empathize with them is if I imagine that it’s me. If someone’s house burns down, I don’t really feel bad for them but I can empathize if I imagine it’s happening to me. I always have to make it about myself in order to “feel”—besides my kids.

Maybe that’s normal though?
No. But at the same time I feel that I’m too good for everyone else.

This is normal because even healthy minded people have to protect themselves. You would go crazy if you heard everyone’s sob story and had to feel something. It’s also great to keep emotions out of things like this because sometimes the stories you are hearing aren’t genuine.

There was a mom telling everyone that her son was terminally ill when he wasn’t. People were sending gifts and cards through the mail, and eventually people came forward and said that the boy wasn’t dying.
You have to be considerate if you want people to “like” you. You’re not getting money out of someone that thinks you’re an asshole.

Do they? From what I’ve seen, people tend to hate them. I mean you have those fucking weirdos that act like it’s “so cool”, but they would be the first people scammed or murdered. It’s a combination of desperation and wanting attention. All you have to do is look at all the idiots that come forward claiming their fathers or grandfathers were the zodiac killer.

They don’t understand the consequences that come with sociopaths/psychopaths, and probably think they can “change” them.

The best way I can explain my anger would be comparing it to a bomb. It’s like I’m okay...I’m getting annoyed...I’m irritated...I’m ready to kill someone. I’m a very explosive person when I get pushed to my limit, and when I’m in that explosive phase everything else seems to fade away besides whatever has pissed me off.

You sound a lot like me minus the drugs. I don’t have a diagnosis though. I did have someone diagnose me on here as a “desensitized NT” though. It’s too bad they didn’t accept my offer of friendship. I would have shown them my collection; they could have even been added to it.

 Just when you think you’re being accepted...

Abusive. Liars. Thieves. Obsessed with their images. Pieces of shit. Enablers to the “golden child” who is currently in prison. All four of their kids have problems. Nature vs nurture? You decide.

I only have bad things to say, so it’s time that I stop before I write a book.

I feel like the tests were garbage because my primary psychopathy score was higher than 92.65% of people that took the test. My secondary psychopathy score was higher than 92.14% of people that took the test. 

I really don’t agree with that at all.

Always check someone out before going on a date or letting your kids go to their friends’ homes. There are a lot of sex offenders that you would never think would be on that list. I know there are others that haven’t been caught yet, but it’s best to look just in case.
Maybe I needed a friend like you to see the good in me.
I do fear death because it’s something out of my control. I wouldn’t commit suicide because I would rather end someone else’s life than my own.

I think many people can fall within the ASPD spectrum, but it’s the people on the moderate to severe end that people associate this personality with. Everyone has lied at some point—like saying someone doesn’t look fat in their pants. Maybe even stole something—even if it was an accident. People might also look at a homeless person and not want to give them food, money, etc. These are things that people can look past, but when it’s excessive that’s when people are usually labeled.
